current.text: Toronto traded for Kawhi Leonard, and Brandon Ingram left in the deal.
Quickley is a projected starter. He is also in the expected closing five with Barrett, Kawhi, Barnes and Murray-Boyles.
Kawhi takes usage away from Quickley. He should take fewer shots but still have the ball a lot. Without Kawhi he would be a tier higher.
Sean expects the highest-volume three-point season of his career, mostly playing off the ball.
His pull-up and transition three-point shooting was poor last season.
Those pull-up and transition threes need to get back to his career averages.
When Kawhi misses time, he should run more on-ball pick and roll.
He stayed healthier last season than in earlier years.
Tier 7 point guard in both formats. Solid, with limited upside.
He was 58th per game last season. His ESPN ADP is 114, which is bench range in a standard ESPN league.
Lloyd thinks he can return about 15 spots of value over his draft position, even with Kawhi there. This call is based on points-league ranks.
Sean predicts 52 wins for Toronto, or 56 to 57 if Kawhi plays 75 games.

durable.text: He is not a classic point guard or a perfect on-ball creator.
He blocks very few shots, even for a guard. A punt BLK team loses little with him.

note: He goes cheap: 1.4 USD average cost on Yahoo and 2.1 USD on ESPN, with ranks of 87 and 90. Our league paid 13 USD for him last season, so he looks like a value pick at single digits (Yahoo value 9, ESPN 3). He fits punt BLK builds best and helps most in threes (2.6) and assists (5.7), while his 43.5% FG% is a small drag. Early in the season, check his shot volume next to Kawhi, whether his three-point volume rises as Sean expects, and whether his pull-up threes get back to his career level.
